description: One input on one step of a wizard. THE FIELD TYPES ARE THE HANDSET'S, not Frappe's: 'photo', 'signature' and 'qr_scan' are things a phone does and a Desk form does not, and a wizard spec written in Frappe fieldtypes would be a spec for the wrong device. Every label carries its translations beside it, because a bilingual crew needs the Spanish to arrive with the field rather than be looked up against a table that drifts.

fields.description: The key this field's answer arrives under. It is what the wizard posts, so it matches the argument name of the endpoint the wizard submits to — a spec whose fieldnames did not would need a translation table on the handset, which is a second place to be wrong.
fields.label: Field Name

fields.description: What the handset draws. `photo`, `signature` and `qr_scan` are the three that make this a mobile spec rather than a form definition; `employee_select` and `asset_select` are pickers the app fills from its own registers.
fields.label: Type
fields.options:
text
long_text
number
date
datetime
select
multi_select
checkbox
photo

qr_scan

employee_select
asset_select

fields.description: The Spanish label. EMPTY IS REPORTED RATHER THAN FILLED IN: `get_wizard_definition` returns the English with a flag saying it was not translated, so a gap is visible to whoever maintains the wizard instead of invisible to the worker who hits it.
fields.label: Label (Spanish)

fields.description: The sentence under the field that says what a good answer looks like. On a discipline or accident wizard this is where 'be specific — dates, times, what was said' lives, and it is the difference between a usable record and 'attitude problem'.
fields.label: Help (English)

fields.description: For a select: the choices, as JSON. Either a list of strings, or a list of objects with `value`, `label_en` and `label_es` — the second where the choices themselves need translating, which on a farm they usually do.
fields.label: Options (JSON)

fields.description: A regular expression the answer has to match. Sent to the handset to check locally — a wizard that only found out at submission that a VIN was malformed would have made somebody walk back to the machine.
fields.label: Pattern

fields.description: Show this field only when the condition holds, as JSON: {"field": "medical_treatment", "not_equals": "None"}. CONDITIONAL LOGIC IS DATA rather than a rule the app carries, which is the whole reason a new wizard needs no release.
fields.label: Visible If (JSON)

fields.description: The argument name this answer is posted under, where it differs from `fieldname`. Rarely needed and here for the case that matters: two steps collecting into one endpoint whose argument names collide.
fields.label: Target Argument

name: Wizard Field
